issues.failure_explanation: The only justification given for $\capacity(\Gamma_n^{\spec}(A))\downarrow\capacity(\spec(A))$ is right-continuity of capacity along decreasing sequences $K_n\downarrow K$. Assumption (S1) does not make the covers nested; it only gives $\spec(A)\subset\Gamma_n^{\spec}(A)$ and Hausdorff-type error bounds $E_n^{\spec}(A)\to0$. So the invoked result is applied outside its hypothesis. (Capacity is not continuous under Hausdorff convergence in general, so some argument is needed.)

failure_location.quote: The capacity is right-continuous as a set function, meaning that for compact sets $K_n, K$ with $K_n\downarrow K$, one has $\capacity(K_n)\downarrow\capacity(K)$. Hence, we can compute the capacity of each output set $\Gamma_n^{\spec}(A)$ to obtain a $\Pi_1^A$ algorithm.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Argue via $\spec(A)\subset\Gamma_n^{\spec}(A)\subset\spec(A)+\overline{B}_{E_n}(0)$: capacity is monotone, and $\spec(A)+\overline{B}_{\epsilon}(0)\downarrow\spec(A)$ as $\epsilon\downarrow0$, so right-continuity applies to the fattened sets and yields convergence from above.
issues.overall_effect: The $\Pi_1^A$ classification of $\Xi_{\mathrm{cap}}$ in cor_assumI_lims (and the derived $\Pi_2^A$ in cor_assumII_extra_lims) is unsupported as written; the conclusion is nevertheless true.
issues.title: Right-continuity of capacity invoked for non-nested covers
issues.why_classification: A two-line local argument restores the claim with no change to the algorithm or classification.

issues.failure_explanation: Under (S1) the available information is $M_n(A)\uparrow\Xi_{\mathrm{cc}}(A)$, so the natural tower $\Gamma_{n_2,n_1}=1$ iff $\max_{n\le n_1}M_n(A)\le n_2$ has $\Gamma_{n_2}(A)=1$ iff $\Xi_{\mathrm{cc}}(A)\le n_2$, which converges to $\Xi^{\mathrm{dec}}_{\mathrm{cc}}(A)$ from below ($\Sigma_2^A$), not from above. Moreover a $\Pi_2^G$ tower cannot exist for the class $\Omega_{\mathrm{DS}}^{(S1)}$: alternating between periodic potentials (finite components, where all $\Gamma_{j}$ must equal 1) and $\mathcal{C}$-type potentials (whose covers exhibit arbitrarily many wide gaps, forcing $\Xi_{\mathrm{cc}}\ge k$), the paper's own prefix-consistency construction yields a limit operator with infinitely many components for which $\Gamma_{j,n_1}=1$ for infinitely many $n_1$ for every $j$, contradicting $\Gamma_j\downarrow0$. No algorithm is given for the claimed $\Pi_2^A$ direction.

issues.failure_explanation: The algorithm (S2_cover_alg) removes balls $D(w,\widehat{\Phi}_{n_1}(n_2;w,A))$ for all grid points $w$ with $|w|\le n_1$, and $\Phi_{n_1}\ge\mathrm{dist}(\cdot,\spec(A))$ is only an upper bound converging uniformly on compacts. For $|w|>L$ (near $\pm n_1$) the overestimate $\Phi_{n_1}(w,A)-\mathrm{dist}(w,\spec(A))$ is uncontrolled, and a ball of overestimated radius around a far grid point can contain points of $\spec(A)$. The proof silently restricts to $G_{1/n_2,L}$. Counterexample satisfying every requirement of (S2) (including monotonicity in $n$): $\Phi_n(z,A)=\mathrm{dist}(z,\spec(A))+|z|^2/n$. Then for $w=n_1$ the radius exceeds $2n_1-\max\spec(A)-1$, so $D(w,\cdot)\supset\spec(A)$ and $\Gamma_{n_2,n_1}^{\spec}(A)\cap\spec(A)=\emptyset$ for all large $n_1$; the limit set is not a cover, contradicting $\spec(A)\subset\Gamma_{n_2}^{\spec}(A)$. Even for the concrete $\Phi_n$ of thm:added-1 the eventual constancy and the monotonicity in $m$ claimed in fractal_dim_final require an argument about far grid points that is absent.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Modify the construction so far grid points cannot over-drill, e.g. cap hole radii at a fixed constant (radius $\min\{\widehat{\Phi}_{n_1}(n_2;w,A),1\}$), then redo the eventual-constancy and monotonicity arguments; alternatively strengthen (S2) to global uniform convergence and prove it for the $\Phi_n$ of thm:added-1 (which does hold via a bounded-truncation-error estimate).
issues.overall_effect: All (S2) classifications rest on lem:cover1 through the covers (S2_cover_alg); as stated for general (S2) data the lemma is false, so thm_warm_up2, cor_assumII_extra_lims and fractal_dim_final (including its monotonicity claim used for the $\Pi_2^A$ upper box-counting result) are unsupported.
issues.title: Covering lemma ignores holes drilled at far-out grid points where $\Phi_{n_1}$ has not converged
issues.why_classification: The lemma is false as stated and the algorithm must be altered or the hypothesis strengthened, but a contained fix preserves every downstream classification.

issues.failure_explanation: (S1) requires each interval of the cover to intersect $\spec(A)$; this is what gives $M_n(A)\le\Xi_{\mathrm{cc}}(A)$ and hence the from-below ($\Sigma$) classification of $\Xi_{\mathrm{cc}}$. Lemma lem:cover1 only establishes $\spec(A)\subset\Gamma_{n_2}^{\spec}(A)\subset\spec(A)+B_{2/n_2}(0)$, and 'enlarging the intervals' cannot create intersections with the spectrum. That every component of $\Gamma_{n_2}^{\spec}(A)$ meets $\spec(A)$ is true for this specific construction (grid points within $1/n_2$ of the spectrum drill no holes, so unremoved points connect to the nearest spectral point) but this needs an argument that is not given.

failure_location.quote: By enlarging the intervals of $\Gamma_{n_2,n_1}^\spec(A)$ as necessary, we can ensure that the sequence $\{\Gamma_{n_2}^\spec\}$ satisfies the requirements of \textbf{(S1)}, apart from being an arithmetic algorithm.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a short lemma: if $x\in\Gamma_{n_2}^{\spec}(A)$ lies in a gap, the nearest grid point has $\widehat{\Phi}(n_2;w,A)=0$, so no hole separates $x$ from the nearest point of $\spec(A)$; hence each component of $\Gamma_{n_2}^{\spec}(A)$ meets $\spec(A)$.
issues.overall_effect: The $\Sigma_2^A$ classification of $\Xi_{\mathrm{cc}}$ under (S2) in cor_assumII_extra_lims is unsupported as written; other entries do not use the intersection property.
issues.title: Unproven that every interval of the drilled cover meets the spectrum ((S1) requirement)
